ai.description: The Darjeeling Caecilian reaches 30–40 cm. It is dark violet to brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and 280–300 primary annuli. It possesses a terminal shield and small, embedded scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis sikkimensis* is distinguished by its distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the head to the tip of the tail, unlike many other Indian species.
ai.habitat: The Darjeeling Caecilian inhabits moist, subtropical forests and tea plantations in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at altitudes between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Darjeeling Caecilian is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through moist soil to hunt for earthworms and small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis sikkimensis* is oviparous, laying 15–30 eggs in terrestrial burrows near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females guarding the clutch.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis sikkimensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Darjeeling Caecilian emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic clicks or chirps, typically heard near streams or damp soil within its humid forest habitat.
